subtitle: Lesson 9 · Finding What Smart Pointers Miss

eyebrow: All four compile cleanly and may "work" at first

steps.label: Double-free
steps.sub: delete called twice on one pointer

steps.label: Buffer overrun
steps.sub: reading or writing past an array's end

eyebrow: Both undefined behavior, both silent at first
caption: Both read and re-release memory that's already been freed.

code:
double prices[3] = {100.1, 100.2, 100.3};

std::cout << prices[5];  // out of bounds
caption: May silently corrupt unrelated memory instead of crashing where it should.
Reports the misuse with a full stack trace, instead of corrupting silently.

steps.label: AddressSanitizer
steps.sub: built into GCC/Clang, fast, needs recompiling

steps.label: Valgrind memcheck
steps.sub: no recompile needed, slower, finds leaks

steps.label: Run in CI
steps.sub: routinely, not just after something looks broken
